options.text: A collection that can hold any type of object

items.explanation: The type parameter <Staff> says the sequence contains Staff items.

misconceptions.a: The whole point of the generic parameter is that it is NOT 'anything' — it is specifically Staff.

items.stem: A Synnduit feed declares `IEntityCollection<Staff> LoadEntities()`. What does the `<Staff>` tell you?

options.text: The collection returned holds Staff entities
The method takes a Staff as a parameter
Staff is the name of the feed class
Only one Staff record is returned

items.explanation: IEntityCollection<Staff> is a collection of Staff — the snapshot the feed returns.

misconceptions.d: A collection can hold many items; the generic parameter is the element type, not a count.

items.stem: In `Dictionary<string, Staff>`, what do the two type parameters represent?

options.text: The key type (string) and the value type (Staff)
Two versions of the same Staff

items.explanation: Dictionary<K,V> maps keys of type K to values of type V — here string keys to Staff values.

items.stem: In one sentence, what is the difference between `IEntityCollection<Staff>` and `IEntityCollection<Student>`?
rubric: Same generic collection type, different element type
One holds Staff entities, the other holds Student entities
items.sampleAnswer: They are the same kind of Synnduit collection, but one contains Staff entities and the other contains Student entities — the type parameter is the only difference.
